title: UML class diagrams
idea: A UML class diagram shows a system's classes, their fields and methods, and how the classes relate, before you write the code.
points: A class box has three parts: name, fields, then methods.
`+` marks public, `-` private and `#` protected members.
Line style, arrowhead and diamond tell you the kind of relationship.
Numbers like `1` or `0..*` at line ends give the multiplicity.

hero.title: A small shop as a class diagram

edges.label: places 0..*
edges.caption: Association, a plain arrow: a `Customer` knows its orders. `0..*` means zero or more.

edges.label: ◆ owns 1..*
edges.caption: Composition: real UML puts a filled diamond on the `Order` end. The order creates its line items; they die with it.

edges.label: refers to
edges.caption: Association: many line items point at one `Product`, which lives on its own.

edges.label: uses
edges.caption: Dependency, a dashed arrow: `Order` only uses a `PaymentMethod` it is given to pay.

edges.label: implements
edges.caption: Realisation: `CardPayment` implements the interface. Real UML ends this dashed line in a hollow triangle, not an arrow.

code.title: The diagram as text
code.caption: Class diagrams show structure; sequence diagrams show calls over time. Here, Mermaid `classDiagram`: `*--` composition, `..>` dependency, `<|..` realisation.

code.title: The diagram in code
code.caption: How two relationships look in JavaScript. `Order` builds its own `LineItem` objects; `Product` is created outside and shared.

pitfalls: In UML `#` means protected, not JavaScript's `#private`; use `-` for private fields.
Draw a filled diamond only when the whole truly owns the part's lifetime.
Draw only the classes and members the discussion needs, not every getter.

quiz.q: `Invoice` creates its `Line` objects itself and no one else holds them. Which relationship is that?
quiz.why: The lines are created by the invoice and cannot outlive it. A part whose lifetime the whole controls is composition.

takeaway: Boxes show classes; line style shows how strongly they are tied.
